name: p06-salted-commitment
proposal: V13-08 erasure receipt; V13-05 cross-border fingerprints
open_question: Should a salted commitment be an evidence format in its own right, so a record can point at personal data without carrying it, and only a party holding the salt can check what it points at?
description: A record of a completed forget request cites a commitment to the item, not the item. The checker's policy does not list the salted-commitment format.
proposed: Same state for a checker without the salt, by design: the core digest rule is unchanged and -02's 'no salted or hiding form of digest' stays true of the core. A checker that holds the salt and lists the format can verify the commitment and release the record. The salt, and anything a fingerprint of personal data counts as, stays with the controller.
status: PROPOSAL: not draft text. For discussion at IETF 127.
